/-!
# Erdős Problem 905

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/905](https://www.erdosproblems.com/905)
- [KhNi79] Khadzhiivanov, N. G. and Nikiforov, S. V., *Solution of a problem of P. Erdős about the
  maximum number of triangles with a common edge in a graph*. C. R. Acad. Bulgare Sci. (1979),
  1315-1318.
-/

namespace Erdos905

open Finset

/--
Every graph with $n$ vertices and $>n^2/4$ edges contains an edge which is in at least $n/6$
triangles.

A conjecture of Bollobás and Erdős. This was proved independently by Edwards (unpublished) and
Khadzhiivanov and Nikiforov [KhNi79].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos905.lean"]
theorem erdos_905 (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (#G.edgeFinset : ℝ)) :
    ∃ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, (n : ℝ) / 6 ≤ (#(G.trianglesContaining e) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos905

review.notes:
The sole declaration, Erdos905.erdos_905, faithfully states the source. Both divisions are real-valued, edges are unordered and loopless, and trianglesContaining counts distinct three-vertex cliques containing the selected edge. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved the arithmetic equivalences and impossibility of the hypothesis for n ≤ 2, checked concrete boundary examples, and computationally tested every labelled simple graph through six vertices. In bridge.lean, I proved that the triangle count equals the number of common neighbors for an actual edge. Both experiment files compile, and the semantic-check lemmas have no sorryAx dependencies.

The source records PROVED (LEAN), consistent with the metadata. The linked proof contains no explicit sorry or custom axioms; its stronger intermediate bound n < 6 * maxTriangleDegree suffices for the repository's real-valued conclusion. However, it targets Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 and does not compile unchanged under the installed 4.33.1, so I did not independently revalidate its proof in its original environment. This is not evidence of a status defect. The original 1979 paper was not retrieved; the exact website statement and the relevant primary 2004 paper were read.
